Debugging is twice as hard as writing the code in the first place. Therefore, if you write the code as cleverly as possible, you are, by definition, not smart enough to debug it.
Beautiful is better than ugly. Explicit is better than implicit. Simple is better than complex. Readability counts.
Rubber duck debugging: explain your code line by line to a rubber duck, and the bug will usually reveal itself before you finish.
